title: Salian Franks
capsule: The Salian Franks were a Frankish group first attested in Roman records around 358 CE when Julian the Apostate, governing Gaul as Caesar, campaigned against them and settled them as foederati in Batavia and Texandria in the lower Rhine delta. From this base, Salian leaders including Chlodio expanded south into the Scheldt-Somme corridor in the early 5th century, and the Salian line culminated in Clovis I (r. 481–511), who united Frankish tribes, defeated the Roman governor Syagrius at Soissons in 486, crushed the Visigoths at Vouillé in 507, and converted to Christianity. Clovis's victories effectively established Frankish dominance over most of Gaul, and his dynasty—the Merovingians—governed the Frankish kingdom for the next two and a half centuries. The terminal date of 510 reflects the consolidation of Clovis's Frankish kingdom, after which the Salians as a distinct sub-group lose historical definition.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Salians' early territorial footprint in the 4th–5th centuries is poorly documented; the polygon reconstructs only a broad zone from Roman military and law-code sources.
